last_assistant_message:
Everything checks out. Here's the report for Master.

## Root cause

Two independent, disagreeing session_id-inference implementations in the eval-harness hooks:

- `hook_utils.infer_session_id()` (used by `eval-turn-start.py`, `eval-turn-stop.py`, and `eval-agent-start.py`'s own hand-copy) read `memory/sessions/index.json`'s **`started`** field.
- `post-tool-use.py`'s `get_session_id()` (and `close-eval-record.py`) read the same file's **`id`** field instead.

Same session, two different string formats depending on which hook asked. Compounding it: `eval-turn-start.py` fires on `UserPromptSubmit`, before boot's own Session Index step appends today's entry — so it can (and did) read a stale, never-closed prior session (Aug 25 17:14:37, `closed: null` to this day). That produced the P00Y9T (stale session_id, Knox's fork misattributed as a boot step), MWOCUW (real boot execution, orphaned as a standalone agent record because it couldn't link back), and WL89IY (a near-empty duplicate created by post-tool-use.py's fallback path when it couldn't find P00Y9T under its own session_id format).

I verified via a claude-code-guide lookup — not assumption — that Claude Code's hook payload carries a guaranteed, session-stable `session_id` on every relevant event. `eval-tool-failure.py`'s own comment claiming otherwise was wrong.

## Fix

Every hook-triggered call site now reads `payload["session_id"]` directly instead of inferring from `memory/sessions/index.json` — no more race, no more format disagreement. The memory-index path survives only as a fallback for payload-less CLI scripts, and now consistently prefers `id` over `started`. Also hardened `post-tool-use.py`'s overwrite guard to refuse touching a `type:"agent"` stub (previously it only guarded against a disagreeing `type:"workflow"` name) — a risk that gets *more* likely now that every hook-opened record in a session shares one true session_id. Files touched: `systems/eval-harness/hook_utils.py`, `.claude/hooks/{eval-turn-start,eval-turn-stop,eval-agent-start,post-tool-use,eval-tool-failure}.py`, `systems/eval-harness/schema.md`. All re-verified with `py_compile`; `infer_session_id()` smoke-tested directly.

## Consolidation

Canonical record: `eval-20260828T140308-WL89IY.json` — status success, started 13:58:56Z, completed 14:03:53.14Z (MWOCUW's real completion), duration 296.75s. Real subagent data (3,976,036 in / 1,158 out tokens, $1.697209) merged in as `subagents[]`; the guardrail pass and the one tool failure merged from P00Y9T; the guardrail-checkpoint assertion now correctly passes. Knox's plaud-ingest fork and the 3 other plaud-discover-fix records are noted by reference in a `related_records` field, **not** merged into boot's cost — that's a genuinely separate workflow's own eval trail.

Archived (not deleted) to `systems/eval-harness/runs/_archived/2026-08-28-boot-consolidation/`: P00Y9T, 0LKM88, MWOCUW, RW2RNP, 8SKFKO, 68E9WF. Confirmed Aug 25 and Aug 27 records untouched.

Tracked in `evolutions/.pending-changes.json` as `work-20260828-boot-eval-session-id-consolidation`; full write-up in `memory/working/rigby-boot-eval-consolidation-2026-08-28.md`.

Not done: didn't run a live end-to-end boot to observe one clean record land in practice (visible tomorrow), didn't touch the still-open Aug 25 session entry in memory/sessions/index.json (moot now, but flagging), and didn't commit — per `skills/git/SKILL.md`, that's a separate step someone runs next covering all files listed above.
